comments.text: Preserve X and Y, bank out I/O and copy twelve pages from RAM $D000–$DBFF to $1000–$1BFF, then four pages from $DC00–$DFFF to $0400–$07FF. Bank the KERNAL and I/O back in, restore Y and X and jump to $1000.
Copy Y plus one pages, starting at the source and destination encoded in the operands at $02DC–$02DD and $02DF–$02E0. Increment the high operand bytes after each page; X wraps through all 256 bytes.

Store A at $0811 and return if $804A is zero. Otherwise call $083A to update the vertical offset and add it to $0811. If the offset at $0810 then equals zero, clear $804A and copy 40 bytes from $A07C to $4400 and 40 bytes from $A0A4 to $4428, in descending index order. Return.

If $804C is zero and $0810 is below $2A, increment $0810 and the five sprite Y operands at $8EFB, $8F2A, $8F3E, $8E8C and $8E78. If $804C is 2 and $0810 is nonzero, decrement the same six bytes. For any other $804C value leave them unchanged. Add $0810 to $0811 using byte arithmetic and return. The scroll-down boundary at $A14B sets $804A when its row pointer reaches $1000; the up and down input routines at $AE17 and $AE4B change $804C.

Write 1 to the VIC interrupt status register, call the sound update at $E13A, and jump to the interrupt restore at $8D69. The outcome-screen setup at $0AF6 installs $088C in the interrupt vector and enables the VIC interrupt. These bytes match the entry and play snapshots; their load origin remains open.

Read CIA 1 port A bit 4 until it is high, then wait until it is low, and jump to the sound-state clear routine. Bit 4 is the active-low joystick-port-2 fire line; CIA port configuration can affect the read.
One 120-byte, space-padded message passed to $0AF6 by the success path at $0897. It praises the player, says enough slime was collected to analyse, and asks for fire to continue.
One 120-byte, space-padded retry message passed to $0AF6 by $0ACC. The routine writes the remaining-chances digit into $09A0 and chooses the byte at $09AD before displaying the message.
One 120-byte, space-padded message passed to $0AF6 by $0AF2. It asks what kind of Ghostbuster would quit, then asks for fire.
One 120-byte, space-padded failure message passed to $0AF6 by $0AEB. It says not enough slime was collected, refers to Vigo, and asks for fire.

Save X and Y into the low and high bytes of the source operand at $0B5C, disable interrupts, install $088C at the interrupt vector, clear bit 7 of VIC control 1, stop CIA 1 timer A, acknowledge and enable the VIC interrupt, set the background to zero, and re-enable interrupts. Select VIC bank and memory settings, clear the sprite enable register, fill $0400–$07FF with $20 and $D800–$DBFF with $0F, and copy 120 source bytes as three 40-character rows to $0540, $0590 and $05E0. For each byte at least $40, subtract $60 with the carry left by CMP; copy smaller bytes unchanged. Callers supply the source pointer in X/Y for the success, retry, quit and failure texts. The interrupt and bank settings are part of the display setup.
